# S5 — Bound writable container layers and alarm on exited-container debris

## Why
Writable container layers live inside `/var/lib/docker/overlay2` and grow independently of
BuildKit cache and image layers. Today nothing measures them and nothing names them: on
2026-09-02 the only signal was `rebar-root-disk-pressure` ("root disk high"), which cannot say
which of the generators grew. This is the last per-accumulator cap under ADR 0112.

## Mechanism decision, with the evidence

The ticket offers a runtime storage quota "when compatible", else a bounded reaper. **The
quota is NOT compatible on this host, and the reaper is what ships.**

Docker's overlay2 `--storage-opt size=` (and its `storage-opts: ["overlay2.size=…"]` daemon
default) is accepted *only* when the filesystem backing `/var/lib/docker` is XFS mounted with
the `pquota` option; otherwise the daemon refuses with `--storage-opt is supported only for
overlay over xfs with 'pquota' mount option`. `/var/lib/docker` is on this box's ROOT
filesystem, and XFS reads quota options at MOUNT time and refuses to enable them on a remount
— so it needs `rootflags=pquota` on the kernel command line and a REBOOT. That is the SAME
constraint S4 (`2ba3`) hit for `/var/tmp`, re-derived for this mechanism and binding here too.
A reboot is a scheduled Gerrit outage a deploy tick may not take. Two further limits even
after the reboot: the quota is PER-CONTAINER, not an aggregate ceiling over the share, and it
applies at container creation, so every live service must be recreated to acquire one.

So this story does what S4 did: ship the mitigation, publish which regime the box is in, and
put the operator steps in the runbook rather than asserting a ceiling that does not exist.

## What the reaper does NOT guarantee — stated, not glossed

1. **It cannot reclaim a RUNNING container's writable layer at all.** Only exited/dead
   containers are removable, so for the live compose set this story delivers MEASUREMENT AND
   AN ALARM, not a bound. The only thing that would bound them is the per-container quota
   above, which is reboot-gated. This is a sharper limitation than S4's fill rate and is said
   first.
2. **For the debris it does bound, the bound is `cap + fill_rate x interval`, not `cap`.** At
   the 2 GiB share and a 300 s timer period a sustained net fill above ~7.2 MB/s exceeds the
   share before the reaper next runs; this gp3 volume does 125 MB/s baseline, ~17x that.
3. Nothing that exited inside the grace window (default 900 s) is ever removed, so a burst of
   fresh exits is unreclaimable by design. When it cannot get under the share it says so.

## Safety — proved against the live set, not asserted

`docker container prune --filter until=…` CANNOT express what this host needs: its filter set
is `until` and `label`, with no name filter. `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` starts the mcp
blue-green backends with a bare `docker run` that compose never sees, and reaps them itself in
`mcp_retire_sweep` under a guard this reaper cannot replicate — it reads the nginx upstream
include and REFUSES to reap an exited container that is still the live backend, because
`--restart always` would otherwise have restored it. Reaping one anyway is bug `9ea3` exactly:
a transient exit became a permanent 502 on 2026-09-02. So the reaper enumerates candidates and
removes them individually instead, and spares three overlapping sets:

* anything carrying `com.docker.compose.project` (gerrit, review-bot, opcert, compose-mcp-1);
* anything carrying the `rebar.service` label (`mcp_run_new`'s stable service identity);
* anything whose name matches `^(rebar-mcp|compose-mcp-1)` — `mcp_managed`'s own regex, so the
  two agree by construction.

Two further daemon-enforced guarantees, not shell logic: candidates come from
`docker ps -a --filter status=exited --filter status=dead`, which never lists a running
container; and removal is `docker rm` WITHOUT `-f`, which the daemon refuses for a running
container (the same precedent `mcp_retire_image` already relies on for images). No `-v` and no
`--volumes` is ever passed, so named and bind volumes are untouched, and
`docker system prune` is never used.

## Observability (S2's publish-or-stay-silent rule)

`observability.sh` §2i, from the SAME single `docker system df` call §2f already makes — the
format string gains `{{.Reclaimable}}` rather than adding a second daemon walk:

* `container_writable_bytes` — the Containers row Size, all writable layers.
* `container_exited_bytes` — the Containers row Reclaimable, i.e. stopped containers' layers.
* `container_writable_used_percent` — `pct_of_cap` (S3's helper, reused) against the share.
* `container_reaper_active` — 1/0 heartbeat, published on EVERY tick including its 0 path.
* `container_quota_enforceable` — 1/0: is the kernel ENFORCING XFS project quota on the Docker
  root filesystem, i.e. could a per-container ceiling exist at all.

Each non-heartbeat reading publishes ONLY on a successful measurement; an unparseable row
publishes nothing, and the breaching alarm pages on the silence rather than a fabricated 0.

## Alarms (Terraform, `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`)

* `rebar-container-writable-usage-high` on `container_writable_used_percent` > 85.
* `rebar-container-reaper-not-active` on `container_reaper_active` < 1. **This is the S4
  finding pre-empted**: without it a silently-dead timer leaves usage reading nominal while
  nothing enforces anything.

Both `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, both wired to `aws_sns_topic.alerts`.
`container_quota_enforceable` is published WITHOUT an alarm, deliberately: its honest value is
0 until the reboot is scheduled, and an alarm that pages continuously is muted within a day.

## One budget, not a second cap

ADR 0112 is explicit that the writable-layer share lives INSIDE the Docker budget, so
`docker-storage-cap.sh` gains a third share — `DOCKER_CONTAINER_WRITABLE_BYTES` (2 GiB) —
carved out of the existing 20 GiB `DOCKER_BUDGET_BYTES`, leaving the image share 13 GiB. No
new independent literal. 2 GiB is a starting point under ADR 0112 decision 6 and is labelled
as such: no writable-layer figure was captured at the 2026-09-02 outage (`docker system df`'s
Containers row was not recorded), so it is sized from the split rather than from a measurement
this repo does not have.

## Scope
In: `container-cap.sh` (budget/reaper/checks, all `--print-*`/`--check-*` side-effect-free),
the observability section, the two alarms, the runbook, and tests. Out: direct
`/var/lib/docker/overlay2` deletion, the BuildKit cap (S2), journald (S3), `/var/tmp` (S4),
and the gate-scratch volume.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Writable-layer growth has a bounded reaper with a documented, quantified limit, and the
      unavailable runtime quota is documented with its exact precondition.
- [ ] Running containers, compose services, `rebar.service`-labelled containers, the mcp
      blue-green set, and all volumes are provably spared; removal is `docker rm` without `-f`.
- [ ] Observability emits writable/exited usage, a cap percentage, and both heartbeats, each
      publishing only on a successful measurement.
- [ ] Terraform declares the two alarms, SNS-wired, `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`.
- [ ] The runbook explains diagnosis/remediation, the quota enablement steps, and forbids
      manual overlay2 deletion.
- [ ] Tests cover reaper command construction and every protected set, metric emission and
      silence, and alarm wiring.
- [ ] Portability: Docker runtime APIs, systemd, and local tests only; no CI-provider trigger.
